findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hard-coded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, console read access, or state file access can read these long-lived credentials and reuse them.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the Lambda environment variables (which contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key rather than a customer-managed CMK with its own access policy, leaving secret material readable by any principal with basic Lambda read permissions.

The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, exposing the function to unpatched vulnerabilities in the runtime and its bundled libraries.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or subnet boundary, which permits data exfiltration if the function is compromised.
